topic: In my country, people tend to arrive late
title: In my country, people tend to arrive late
pt: Foco da aula: diferenças culturais: in my country / people tend to / it’s common to

solo90.name: Pausa

lines.en: Max, you arrived exactly on time for our meeting. Is that normal where you come from?
lines.pt: Max, você chegou exatamente na hora do nosso encontro. Isso é normal de onde você vem?

lines.en: Honestly, it is a little strange. In my country, people tend to arrive late to social events, even twenty minutes late.
lines.pt: Sinceramente, é meio estranho. No meu país, as pessoas costumam chegar atrasadas a eventos sociais, até vinte minutos.

lines.en: Twenty minutes! Here in Texas, that would be rude, especially for a business meeting or a dinner.
lines.pt: Vinte minutos! Aqui no Texas isso seria rude, principalmente numa reunião de negócios ou num jantar.

lines.en: I know. When I arrived in Austin, I was always the last person at parties, and people looked annoyed.
lines.pt: Eu sei. Quando cheguei a Austin, eu era sempre o último nas festas, e as pessoas pareciam incomodadas.

lines.en: People are polite here, so they rarely complain. What other differences have you noticed since you moved?
lines.pt: As pessoas aqui são educadas, então raramente reclamam. Que outras diferenças você notou desde que se mudou?

lines.en: In my country, it is common to greet friends with a kiss on the cheek, and people tend to stand much closer.
lines.pt: No meu país, é comum cumprimentar amigos com um beijo no rosto, e as pessoas costumam ficar muito mais perto.

lines.en: That explains why my neighbour looked surprised! Here, we usually shake hands or give a quick hug, and we keep some distance.
lines.pt: Isso explica por que meu vizinho pareceu surpreso! Aqui geralmente apertamos as mãos ou damos um abraço rápido, e mantemos alguma distância.

lines.en: Yes, I am getting used to it. I am also surprised that people eat dinner so early. Six o’clock seems too early!
lines.pt: Sim, estou me acostumando. Também me surpreende que as pessoas jantem tão cedo. Seis horas me parece cedo demais!

lines.en: Ha! In my family, we eat at six sharp. Maybe that is why I hate it when guests are late and the food gets cold.
lines.pt: Ha! E na minha família jantamos às seis em ponto. Talvez por isso eu odeie quando os convidados atrasam e a comida esfria.

lines.en: I understand. From now on, I will make an effort to be on time, but please be patient with me.
lines.pt: Entendo. Daqui em diante vou me esforçar para ser pontual, mas tenha paciência comigo.

lines.en: Deal. Now let us look at the food stands before the music starts. I have heard the barbecue is excellent.
lines.pt: Combinado. Agora vamos olhar as barracas de comida antes de a música começar. Ouvi dizer que o churrasco daqui é excelente.

facts.big: in my country · people tend to · it’s common to
facts.label: Diferenças culturais
facts.sub: Use In my country, people tend to + verbo base e It’s common to + verbo base para descrever costumes e comparar lugares.

facts.label: As pessoas costumam
facts.sub: In my country, people tend to + verbo base descreve um hábito geral: people tend to arrive late. Com people use tend, não tends. Com he/she use tends: he tends to be late.

facts.label: É comum
facts.sub: It’s common to + verbo base mostra um costume aceito: It’s common to greet friends with a kiss. Pode também usar it’s normal to e it’s usual to.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: “People tend to…” describes a general habit.
items.why: It is not a rule for everyone.

items.s: “It’s common to” is followed by a verb in the base form with to.
items.why: It’s common to greet with a kiss.

items.s: We say “In my country, people tends to arrive late”.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: “People tend to…” describes a general habit. → Verdadeiro (It is not a rule for everyone.)
“It’s common to” is followed by a verb in the base form with to. → Verdadeiro (It’s common to greet with a kiss.)
We say “In my country, people tends to arrive late”. → Falso (People is plural: people tend.)

pages.title: Customs at the fair · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a sunny Saturday at a big fair in Austin. Music plays near the food stands. Max walks in right on time. His friend Hal looks at his watch. Hal is surprised, because Max is usually late. They start to talk about customs.

“Max, you arrived exactly on time for our meeting. Is that normal where you come from?” says Hal. “Honestly, it is a little strange. In my country, people tend to arrive late to social events, even twenty minutes late.” says Max. “Twenty minutes! Here in Texas, that would be rude, especially for a business meeting or a dinner.” says Hal.
